subject: Default log horizon — concrete examples for request vs. generated artifacts
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@silverlinepay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Silverline Security Team <sec@silverlinepay.com>
Date: 2028-08-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (concrete examples)

Hi Olga,

We're pulling together our internal data map and need to be very explicit about what Redwood stores by default. Could you give concrete examples for the following so we can put them in our security questionnaire?

- User-submitted prompt text (e.g., a chat message the user typed)
- Model-generated response (including streaming fragments vs final output)
- Streaming tokens/KV cache artifacts during interactive sessions
- Attachments uploaded as part of a request (PDF/invoice)
- Embeddings/indices generated from user content

If you can provide default retention horizons (days), and any distinctions for EU-residency vs global, that would be ideal. We're on a tight deadline for an audit next week.

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Lee
Security Lead, Silverline Payments

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@silverlinepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-03T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (concrete examples)

Jamie — thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together the short, concrete answers below and attached a small example matrix (retention_examples_silverline.xlsx) plus our public default doc (redwood-default-retention-v2.pdf). High-level summary first, then examples.

Summary (default hosted API):
- Prompts / request payloads: retained for 30 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Model-generated final outputs: retained for 90 days by default to support dispute resolution and customer troubleshooting; streaming fragments are not persisted beyond session unless the API call completes and the final output is stored.
- Streaming tokens / KV cache: ephemeral — kept for up to 7 days in short-term runtime buffers and tombstoned automatically; not indexed or searchable.
- Attachments uploaded with a request: file blobs are stored for 30 days by default (same as request payloads) unless the customer requests a different retention via account settings or contract.
- Embeddings / derived vectors: retained per-account configuration; defaults are 180 days for managed embeddings but can be set longer for Dedicated/Private customers.

Regional nuance: the retention horizon above applies to the account's residency region. If your account is configured for EU residency, the storage and deletion operations occur within the EU. Retention periods remain the same unless we have a contractual exception — in which case we log that exception in the account record.

I'll run this past Marissa and Sean for any legal/compliance caveats and send a short formal answer you can include in the questionnaire. Drive link to the matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-retention-matrix

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-03T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (concrete examples)

Olga / Sean — quick internal note before Olga sends final to Silverline:
- The 30/90/7 split is fine for hosted. Suggest we explicitly call out that for Dedicated customers we can extend the outputs retention to 365 days on request (contracted).
- For embeddings: default shown as 180 days is accurate for managed embeddings; add that customers can opt into 'persistent embeddings' with explicit storage waivers.
- Attachments: make sure we indicate S3 storage class and lifecycle policies (standard -> infrequent -> delete) so they see the operational controls.
- Recommend we include the process to request retention changes (email to security@redwood.ai + sales contact) and mention that changes require audit trail updates.

If Olga wants, I can add a one-paragraph "how to request an exception" to the matrix.

—Marissa

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@silverlinepay.com>
Cc: Silverline Security Team <sec@silverlinepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-03T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: what Redwood keeps by default (concrete examples)

Jamie — following up with the finalized language you can drop into your questionnaire. I've attached the matrix and the public doc for reference. Short version that maps to the items you listed:

1) User-submitted prompt text (example: "Transfer $12k to account X")
- Default retention: 30 days (hosted). Purpose: debugging, abuse detection, quality monitoring.
- Residency: Stored in account region (EU/US/APAC) for the duration.

2) Model-generated response (final output)
- Default retention: 90 days (hosted). Purpose: dispute resolution, audit trails.
- Streaming fragments: not persisted beyond session playback unless the request successfully completes and the final output is recorded.

3) Streaming tokens / KV cache (example: live session prefixes, tokenized frames)
- Default behavior: ephemeral runtime buffers; tombstoned within 7 days. Not indexed, not exported to customer logs by default.

4) Attachments uploaded with request (example: invoice_789.pdf)
- Default retention: 30 days. Blobs stored using account-region buckets; lifecycle policy applied.

5) Embeddings / derived vectors
- Default: 180 days for managed embeddings. For Dedicated customers or under contract we can support persistent embeddings (> 365 days) with documented control and data-processing addendum.

How to change defaults / request an exception:
- Submit a request to security@redwood.ai (please include account id and desired retention); for standard hosted accounts changes can take up to 5 business days to apply; Dedicated/private requires contractual amendment. All changes generate an audit record.

Attachments: retention_examples_silverline.xlsx, redwood-default-retention-v2.pdf
Link to policy: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/data-retention#default-horizon

If you want, we can format the single-paragraph answers for inclusion in Silverline's questionnaire — tell me which fields you need and I'll send a cut-and-paste block.

Best,
Olga

From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@silverlinepay.com>

Thanks — that is exactly what we needed. We'll include the bullets in the audit pack and may reach back if we need contracted exceptions. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Jamie
